MAPPING SYSTEM DOMAIN FROM (−LS, 0), (−π, π) TO (−2LS, 0), (0, π) Here we discuss the equivalence between formulating the system on the interval (−LS, 0) and on the unwrapped interval (−2LS, 0). In the original description, the momentum quantum number spans the full Brillouin zone, k ∈ [−π, π], so that positive and negative momenta correspond to right- and left-moving excitations, respectively. The negative-k sector therefore represents modes propagating toward decreasing spatial coordinates within the interval (−LS, 0). An equivalent description is obtained by extending the system to (−2LS, 0) and restricting the momentum label to k ∈ [0, π]. In this unwrapped representation, the degrees of freedom that were previously associated with negative momenta are reinterpreted as positive-momentum particles originating from the additional spatial segment (−2LS, −LS). Thus, a left-moving excitation in the original formulation is mapped to a right-moving excitation on the enlarged interval, with the direction of propagation encoded in the spatial origin of the mode rather than in the sign of its momentum. The correspondence is one-to-one, ensuring that no degrees of freedom are lost or introduced in passing from one representation to the other. In the new representation, on reflection from the defect at the origin, a particle starts again from x = −2LS with the same momentum. II.
